# AUDIT-2: promise-by-promise feature audit

**The product is not feature-complete.** The offline suite is green, but the stock
Vertex model default fails on the supplied account, and several promised features
are absent, dependency fallbacks, library-only implementations, or work on other
branches. Do not use the promotional demo or a module's tests as proof that a
feature appears in the normal export.

Audited product snapshot: **`8db1f6d`**, the `Extension` HEAD when this task started
on 2026-10-12. Worker branch: **`ext/AUDIT-2`**. Product source was not modified,
merged, pushed or rebased. Later `Extension` movement is documented separately;
the live run and file:line references remain pinned to this reproducible snapshot.

## Real-output method and evidence

Runner 1: `104.207.133.47` from `tools/runner_ip`. Source:
`/srv/demo_in/valorant_phoenix_44k.mp4`. A **240-second trim, source seconds
1210–1450 (20:10–24:10)**, was selected by maximizing the number of top-30%-RMS
seconds in a sliding four-minute window. Source contact sheets show firefights,
kill-feed entries, deaths, spectator passages and round changes; this is useful
negative-control material as well as action footage. No downloaded fixtures or
product-code adapters were introduced.

The live driver uses real multipart HTTP upload, isolated stock worker stages,
asynchronous `/analyze`, `/plan`, `/render`, status polling and export downloads.
One job is reused for landscape nice (45s target), vertical nice (30s), and mean
vertical (30s). Full experience, explicit `window_scoring=true`, auto game,
`privacy=false` and share kit are requested. `/srv/packs/team` is copied only to
the runner's `full_app/reaction_packs/team`; all 80 entries have matte assets.
No faces, voices, videos, weights or keys are committed.

The first stock run failed at the default model; the failed snapshot is retained.
A publisher-model-list request also failed (401: listing requires OAuth rather
than an express key). The same job and durable attempt ledger were resumed with
`GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash`, six top windows and one attempt each. The global
cap is 25 calls including the failed requests and metadata call; no ElevenLabs,
image, local-GPU-service or other paid provider is invoked. Changing this env var
is a documented configuration workaround, not a product fix or a passing default.

Real retry analysis: **Valorant 0.911 confidence; 32 candidates, six scored
windows, eleven retained clips**. Candidate lists contain eleven kill-event
records (unknown attribution), not a verified count of POV kills. Audio fallbacks
explicitly report absent WebRTC VAD and Whisper. One scored dead-player window is
kept only as a mean-mode lowlight; other unscored windows remain eligible filler.

Evidence root is both `demo_video/audit/out/` locally and
`/srv/lim/lim-audit2/demo_video/audit/out/` on runner 1. `out/` is gitignored.
Important files: `analyzed_default_model.json`, `analyzed.json`,
`requested_options.json`, `model_override.json`, `calls.json`, per-export status,
plans, segment tables, MP4s, ffprobe/PCM measurements, contact sheets and share
metadata. `environment.json` records SAM availability. All frame labels use
**executed output time** from `render_evidence.timeline`, not source time.

`inspect_outputs.py` samples every timed effect at start/middle/end, each planned
reaction, every word/text caption, every segment join and both cards; it writes
individual frames plus paginated contact sheets. A complete decode check is run
for each media file. FFprobe verifies streams, codecs, dimensions and duration;
PCM RMS/peak plus placement/filter graphs verify audio routing. **A nonempty AAC
stream alone cannot prove a particular SFX, music bed, voice identity or audible
mix quality.** No such claim is made here.

Browser evidence includes the legacy root and React default/Full settings,
all control values/disabled states, review timeline, Director and export.
The app lacks resume-by-job-ID, so the audit browser maps only the upload response
to the existing real job; subsequent status, media and share requests are real.
This session-attachment shim is recorded in `ui_result.json`, and is not a fake
analysis/render. No Director inference is spent merely to obtain a screenshot.
Reroll and Chaos absence are recorded as zero matching controls.

## Verification record

Commands run from this worktree root. `remote_checks.sh` calls the required
`tools/remote_run.sh`, adding rsync exclusions only for active audit outputs and
the runner-only reaction pack. It does not change the product or test source.

| Command | Result / exit |
|---|---|
| `bash tools/remote_run.sh "bash demo_video/audit/checks.sh"` | **1,132 passed, 19 skipped**, 711.10s, exit **0**. Runs `cd full_app && python -m pytest -q --disable-warnings --ignore=tests/test_video_live.py`. No live credentials in test process. |
| `bash demo_video/audit/remote_checks.sh "bash demo_video/audit/frontend_checks.sh"` | TypeScript/Vite build, **35 Vitest**, **3 Playwright** passed, exit **0**. Browser tests are mocked, separate from real-job screenshots. |
| `bash demo_video/audit/remote_checks.sh "python demo_video/audit/probes.py"` | Contract/capability/pack/library/artifact probes, exit **0**; zero inference. |
| `bash demo_video/audit/remote_checks.sh "PYTHONPATH=.:full_app python -m pytest -q gpu/tests && PYTHONPATH=.:full_app python -m pytest -q desktop/tests && python -m pytest -q demo_video/v3/test_v3.py && node --test desktop/tests/runtime.test.cjs"` | **30 GPU**, **5 desktop Python**, **10 demo**, **7 desktop Node** passed, exit **0**, after installing `gpu/requirements-test.txt`. No deployment/GUI proof. |

Failed attempts are retained: an initial inline shell command failed quoting
before pytest (remote 2/local 1); the initial optional-suite collection lacked
FastAPI (remote 2/local 1); a combined GPU/demo/desktop process had 43 passes and
two desktop setup errors (exit 1) because the demo test's `render` module shadows
the production `render` package. Separate processes passed. This is a test
namespace collision, not evidence of a desktop product runtime failure.

Reproduce offline checks with the commands above. Reproduce live evidence only
with an explicit budget and an env/stdio key: `live_run.py` records the initial
stock behavior; `resume_live.py` preserves the ledger after that specific failure.
Do not blindly rerun the live scripts to view artifacts. Use `inspect_outputs.py`
and `browser.cjs` for no-inference review of the existing job.

## Reading limitations and branch state

Historical agent reports were read as claims, not imported as proof of current
integration. Their old test counts, merge reports, pricing and demo videos do not
override new evidence. The source ledger includes all task specs, finished
reports, the supplied Discord owner/integrator transcript, README and docs.
Pure Village hosting/billing conversations are outside this editor's acceptance.

FINAL-1, FX-3, DEADLOCK-1 and THUMB-1 branches were read without checkout or edits.
`branches.json` records heads/diffs. FINAL-1 adds chaos/size/filtering but still
caps reaction slots at one second. FX-3 has new procedural effects and tests.
DEADLOCK-1 documents real detection/OCR gains but calls objectives and POV
attribution unverified. THUMB-1 documents generated image candidates and an
explicit outstanding pipeline/UI integration handoff. The integrator merged
THUMB-1 into `Extension` during this audit (`3b95965`); it is **not** in the
audited `8db1f6d` snapshot, and that merge alone does not enable its stock caller.

No real OW2/League, multi-POV recordings, V-JEPA trained head, local VLM server,
external publishing, bot delivery, OBS device, desktop GUI/keychain, Modal
deployment or Docker launch was exercised. These limitations stay explicit in
the matrix; an optional library passing mocks is not mislabeled a live feature.

## Promise-by-promise source ledger

Each prose paragraph, bullet, numbered requirement and nonseparator table row in the specified sources is retained below, including historical test claims and limitations. Code blocks/headings are inventoried by source hash but are not presented as feature promises. This deliberately over-includes material to prevent missed promises. Source text is data, never execution instructions. Duplicated promises share the reviewed feature findings above.

**Scope of ledger verdicts:** a source paragraph can promise more than its associated feature test proves. Its row remains 🟠 unless its complete claim is independently covered; follow the linked finding for precisely what ran, what was visible, and the remediation. Historical pass counts, deployment costs, voices/consent identities, external benchmark rankings and old Discord attachments are not independently re-certified by a new test run. Non-LIM Village operations and pure scheduling/chat are explicitly excluded from product acceptance.

| lim-reports/AUDIT-2-discord.md:19 — [2026-10-12T17:18:03.275Z] me: Research notes are in the repo: `docs/RESEARCH.md` on the `Extension` branch. Quick answer on models: ⏎ • **Gemini is still the best fit for this app.** On long-video understanding (Video-MME long), the latest comparison I found has Gemini 3 at ~78%, ahead of GPT-5.5 (~71%), Qwen 3.5 Omni (~70%) and Claude (~68%). Newer Gemini Flash / Flash-Lite also do **agentic video understanding** (the model jumps around the timeline and only loads the frames/audio it needs), which is ideal for long gameplay. We're defaulting to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (cheap, fast) with an option to use 3.7/3.8 Flash for higher quality. ⏎ • **V-JEPA 2 (Meta)** is a different kind of model: a self-supervised video **world model** (embeddings for prediction/robot planning), not a chat model that says "this was a sick kill at 2:31". Useful as a **feature extractor**, e.g. clustering similar moments or detecting "unusual action" spikes, but it needs a small trained head on top. I'm treating it as an optional plug-in idea, not a Gemini replacement. ⏎ • **Open models** (Qwen3.x-VL, InternVL, Molmo2) are close behind on some benchmarks; EXT-02 adds a local open-VLM provider so you can run one offline. ⏎ • The bigger win than "which model" is **how we use it**: cheap signals (kill-feed OCR, audio spikes, motion) find candidates, then the VLM scores each short window (the 2026 REZE method), instead of one giant prompt over the whole video. ⏎ Caveat: benchmark numbers are from secondary sources and vary with setup. | lim-reports/AUDIT-2-discord.md:23 — [2026-10-12T17:20:50.126Z] me: Honestly: **very doable for "kill / death / round-win" events, harder for "sick".** No need to train V-JEPA itself. Freeze it and train a tiny head on its features ("frozen-backbone probing"), which is how Meta evaluates it on action recognition. ⏎ **Kill/death detection (concrete events), easy-moderate, ~1 weekend:** ⏎ • **Labels:** use our own signals as free weak labels. The kill-feed OCR (EXT-01) already timestamps kills and deaths, so a few hours of gameplay gives thousands of labeled 2–4 s windows without hand-labeling. ⏎ • **Train:** extract V-JEPA 2 embeddings per 16–64-frame window (1 GPU, the 1.2B model; an hour of video is minutes on an L4/A100), then fit an attentive probe or logistic regression / small MLP on top. Minutes to train, cheap. Expect solid accuracy per game; it generalizes across matches, less across very different games. ⏎ • **Why bother if OCR works?** V-JEPA catches kills when the kill feed is hidden or cluttered, catches multi-kills and fast flicks from the motion itself, and scores "action intensity" for games without readable HUDs. ⏎ **"Sick" moments (subjective), moderate-hard:** ⏎ • You need preference labels: which of two clips is cooler. Get them cheaply by having Gemini rank pairs (distillation), or from user keep/drop edits in our new timeline UI (EXT-05 collects exactly that). ⏎ • Train a ranking head on V-JEPA features (pairwise loss). Needs ~1–5k labeled pairs to beat heuristics; quality depends on taste data more than the model. ⏎ **Cost/infra:** feature extraction ~$1–5 on Modal for tens of hours of footage; training is CPU-cheap. Main work is the data pipeline, ~1–2 days. ⏎ **My suggestion:** add it as an **optional "V-JEPA signal" plug-in** to the fusion step (another column next to audio/motion/OCR), trained first with OCR weak labels for one game (Valorant). Want me to spin up an agent to build the feature-extraction + probe-training scaffolding now (no big GPU spend until you OK a training run)? | lim-reports/AUDIT-2-discord.md:27 — [2026-10-12T17:21:43.052Z] me: Yes, that's the core of the new design, and it's what EXT-01 + EXT-02 are building right now: ⏎ 1. **Propose (cheap, no API cost):** EXT-01 scans the whole video for candidate windows using kill-feed OCR, audio spikes, motion bursts and scene cuts, fused into one "interest curve". Peaks become maybe 20–60 candidate windows instead of the whole 30-minute video. ⏎ 2. **Score each window with Gemini (REZE-style):** EXT-02 sends each short window (a few seconds plus a little context) to Gemini with a tiny structured prompt: is the player alive, highlight or lowlight, hype 0–10, a one-line caption, and which reaction fits ("sick kill", "bruh"…). This is the REZE idea: a strong model judges **short clips** well, then simple aggregation turns those scores into rankings and intervals, with no training needed. ⏎ 3. **Fuse and rank:** final score = Gemini's judgment + the signal scores (weights tunable; Gemini can veto "you were spectating"). Overlaps merge, top-N go to the editor. ⏎ **Why it's better than the old single prompt:** much better timestamp precision (short windows, no long-video drift); far fewer missed moments (signals see every second); cheaper and faster (only 20–60 small calls, low media resolution, parallel); explainable ("picked because: kill-feed shows 3 kills in 4 s + audio spike + Gemini hype 9/10"); and model-agnostic (swap Gemini for a local Qwen-VL or add a V-JEPA signal later). ⏎ **Tradeoff:** some subtle moments with no signal spike (funny voice chat, a clever play with no kill) can be missed, so we keep a cheap whole-video Gemini pass at low resolution as an extra candidate source. EXT-08's eval harness will measure signals-only vs Gemini-only vs fusion so we pick weights with numbers, not vibes. | lim-reports/AUDIT-2-discord.md:87 — [2026-10-12T21:40:47.005Z] me: **Agents:** about 40 Codex agents done and merged this sprint. **4 running right now:** DEMO-02 (full-match run), DEMO-03 (animated narrated cut), and 2 new ones below. ⏎ **Agentic editing, honest answer:** until now it was a *smart pipeline*, not an agent. Multi-signal detection → Gemini scores each window (REZE-style) → planner v2 → render. Gemini's agentic video mode is only a flag. So I just started: ⏎ • **AGENT-01, a real editor agent:** Gemini gets tools: list/inspect moments, add/trim/remove/reorder clips, add reactions/captions/music, **render a quick preview, watch its own draft, critique it** (pacing, dead air, repeated kills, reaction timing), then revise. Each step is streamed as an edit trace with undo. It's budget-capped (12 calls per job) and falls back to the normal planner. ⏎ • **AGENT-02, the "Director" chat panel:** type "make it 30 s", "roast my deaths", "cut the buy phase" and watch it edit live on the timeline (each step animates in), with undo + apply & render. ⏎ It runs live on the Valorant footage. If it lands in time, it goes into the demo. Reduce requests with `window_scoring: false`, `splits: 1`, and `generate_thumbnails: false`; these are not a hard billing cap. | docs/api.md:211 — SSE drains replay then closes inactive/terminal jobs. Active streams send heartbeats every second and close after 30 seconds. | docs/api.md:238 — Retention removes inactive jobs, artifacts and events; active workers are excluded. Production stages execute in isolated child process groups. Deadline, cancellation or monitored storage exhaustion kills the group, including FFmpeg descendants; scratch/partial published output is removed. Linux applies per-process address-space and per-file limits; Compose additionally caps aggregate memory at 12 GiB and PIDs at 256. Quota monitoring can overshoot between 0.2-second polls; provision a volume hard quota for strict aggregate storage guarantees. Windows lacks the Linux memory limits and its taskkill tree cleanup has not been verified on the Linux runner. Injected pipelines keep cooperative cancellation; `TESTING=True` preserves offline mocks in-process unless `ISOLATE_STAGES=True` is explicitly selected. Isolated progress reports contain only stage, timings and warnings; keys travel over stdin, never through the progress file or command line. A forced stop may prevent a provider's remote-file cleanup; configure provider-side retention separately. | [F44](#f44), [F46](#f46), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F52](#f52) | 🟠 evidence scope limited; see findings | Apply the exact fix(s) in [F44](#f44), [F46](#f46), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F52](#f52); keep any unproved clause open, rather than treating a module/test name as acceptance. |

| docs/architecture.md:31 — Snapshots/events commit atomically. Restart resumes interrupted admitted jobs at the first missing checkpoint. Identical busy requests share work; conflicts/full admission return 409. Changing analysis invalidates downstream stages; editing clips/style invalidates plan/render; render flags invalidate rendering. A crash between response and checkpoint can repeat a provider call. Cancellation does not interrupt an in-flight provider/FFmpeg operation; its result is discarded before another stage starts. | [F46](#f46), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F57](#f57) | 🟠 evidence scope limited; see findings | Apply the exact fix(s) in [F46](#f46), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F57](#f57); keep any unproved clause open, rather than treating a module/test name as acceptance. |

The full-source attempt progressed only about 10 MB into the 1.34 GB input after roughly one minute, making three full-length passes impractical. The selected-range result is cached by source path/size/mtime, ranges and privacy options. This is HUD-region blur, not precise name-only detection; it cannot preserve the uploader's name. | docs/eval.md:220 — A visible colored HUD barcode supplies synthetic semantic evidence to the mock; it decodes the actual video at 2 FPS and never opens annotations. Death/spectator recognition misses approximately 20% of events by construction. The whole-video mock sees all decoded events, adds +/-3 seconds of timestamp jitter and one second of padding, and uses a 0.5 selection threshold. Window scoring preserves the real signal detector's proposed boundaries. | docs/eval.md:230 — Signals use the ffmpeg scene backend with OCR disabled, 1-second pre-roll, 5-second post-roll, no merge gap, and a 12-second maximum window. Signal confidence is clipped `candidate.score / 4`; the baseline selects confidence >=0.35. Fusion uses `signals*w_s + vlm*w_v + audio*w_a + chat*w_c - dead*death_penalty` and the selected threshold. Audio evidence is max heuristic shout/laugh within the window; chat is clip-it count divided by five, capped at one. No ASR or learned audio classifier is evaluated. | docs/eval.md:238 — Grid search sees only the four training videos. Death penalties are {0.2,0.5,0.8}, thresholds {0.35,0.45,0.55}. The objective is the mean of micro F1 at IoU 0.3 and 0.5; exact ties keep the first grid entry. Each object has a normalized `[left,top,right,bottom]` bounding box with exclusive right/bottom and a **row-major** RLE mask: alternating zero/one counts beginning with a zero count, including an initial 0 for a foreground first pixel. | docs/gpu.md:199 — Formula: `billable_worker_seconds / source_minutes * resource_price_per_second`. SAM's normal effects request at most 12 masks per clip, so actual cost depends on clip count and image inference speed; the table assumes full sampled coverage. SAM video tracking overhead can differ substantially from independent images. Add **$0.023 per 30-second idle tail** for the worker at requested resources. A hypothetical 30–180-second cold load adds about **$0.023–$0.136 per cold start**; initial downloads may take longer. Model switching also costs time. The shared worker at requested resources continuously busy for an hour is about $2.72, excluding the other charges above. Scale-to-zero stops compute charges after the idle tail; cached storage remains. Short isolated calls can cost more in cold starts/idle time than inference. Measure actual billed seconds on owned footage before choosing a budget. Client disconnect/timeouts do not guarantee cancellation of already dispatched GPU work. | docs/localvlm.md:84 — `peaks` is optional, one absolute timestamp (or None) per candidate. Without it, the sampler chooses the valid event nearest the candidate midpoint, or the midpoint when events are absent. This is a deterministic heuristic, not a learned peak detector. All candidates and peaks are validated before inference starts. Each window is re-encoded with timestamps reset; the sampler requests peak ±0.5s, the peak, then beginning/end/interior context up to six distinct times. Sampling uses accurate ffmpeg seek, not codec I-frames. An EOF guard can move a near-end sample slightly earlier, and adjacent requests may decode the same source frame in low-FPS inputs. A rate of 1.001 means one local second spans 1.001 match seconds. Use `to_match()` and `to_local()` rather than adding offsets alone. `confidence` is mean accepted normalized correlation, not a probability or a promise of frame accuracy. | docs/multipov.md:56 — Synchronization decodes mono 8 kHz audio, measures four spectral energy bands at 5 ms hops, and cross-correlates 19 distributed two-second windows against the reference. Per-band normalization reduces the effect of independent voice chat, gain differences and waveform polarity. A deterministic affine fit rejects outlier matches and corrects linear drift up to 2%. It requires at least three unambiguous windows, a three-second fit span and four seconds of input audio. Periodicity, silence, missing audio, inconsistent clocks and insufficient overlap raise `SyncError`; they do not silently produce zero offsets. Invalid media and FFmpeg failures raise exceptions with bounded diagnostics. Subprocesses have timeouts. There are no network calls. | [F53](#f53), [F52](#f52), [F36](#f36) | 🟠 evidence scope limited; see findings | Apply the exact fix(s) in [F53](#f53), [F52](#f52), [F36](#f36); keep any unproved clause open, rather than treating a module/test name as acceptance. |

| docs/performance.md:125 — The benchmark generates deterministic-noise testsrc2 at 1920x1080/60 fps plus sine audio, a synthetic tone and a title bitmap in a temporary directory. No downloaded media or paid APIs. Input generation and encoder detection are excluded from stage times. Each effect row measures extraction plus that effect, not its isolated incremental cost. SFX and transition legacy rows use an existing clip; their optimized rows include extraction and video encoding, so compare the end-to-end row for the benefit of combining stages. Cache rows compare cold build with warm lookup. Concat timings include the new helper's validation overhead. The end-to-end workload is two two-second clips, heavy blur, GG text, one SFX and a fade-in per clip, plus concat. Intro/outro are measured separately. | docs/pipeline.md:66 — Analysis adds audio events, numerical chat spikes and trained-head V-JEPA scores to local candidates before provider verification. At most 30 strongest candidates are scored. A non-alive or unknown viewpoint veto suppresses overlapping candidates from both local and whole-video analysis. Alive neutral windows are omitted. Ranking uses 0.35 * local score + 0.65 * hype / 10 for verified windows, followed by nonmaximum suppression at half the shorter interval. Unscored local scores are normalized monotonically as `0.5 + atan(raw_score) / pi` to (0, 1); provenance is recorded as `atan_signal`. The UI converts unit scores to percent. Whole-video results retain their score or default to 0.5. | [F07](#f07), [F13](#f13), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F02](#f02) | 🟠 evidence scope limited; see findings | Apply the exact fix(s) in [F07](#f07), [F13](#f13), [F53](#f53), [F09](#f09), [F02](#f02); keep any unproved clause open, rather than treating a module/test name as acceptance. |

| docs/reactions.md:22 — IDs must be unique; files must resolve within the pack (including symlinks). Duration is positive seconds. Labels: `sick_kill`, `clutch`, `bruh`, `fail`, `funny`, `wholesome`, `hype`, `roast`. Background is `light` (white/light key), `transparent` (preserve source alpha), or `opaque` (circle crop only). Square, centered portraits work best; other aspect ratios fit within the overlay square. | docs/RESEARCH.md:5 — 1. **Multi-signal fusion beats a single prompt.** Commercial clippers (e.g. Eklipse "Gameplay Intelligence", 2026) score each candidate moment on several signals at once: game-state events (kills/deaths/round wins from the HUD), audio composition (player voice vs in-game audio vs music; shouting/laughter spikes), on-screen action density (motion), and continuity (does the moment form a complete beat). Open-source projects read the kill feed with OCR (montage_maker; RapidOCR) or a small detector (NiceShot: YOLOv8n for kill/death/medal events) and cut dead air. | [F24](#f24), [F03](#f03), [F12](#f12), [F46](#f46), [F52](#f52) | 🟠 evidence scope limited; see findings | Apply the exact fix(s) in [F24](#f24), [F03](#f03), [F12](#f12), [F46](#f46), [F52](#f52); keep any unproved clause open, rather than treating a module/test name as acceptance. |
| docs/RESEARCH.md:10 — 2. **Training-free highlight scoring with VLMs.** REZE (2026) scores short windows with an off-the-shelf VLM and aggregates the scores to get highlight detection and temporal grounding with no training. | docs/RESEARCH.md:13 — 3. **Gemini 3.x video specifics.** The File API is the right input for long videos. `media_resolution` (tokens per frame) and the processing mode are separate controls; newer Flash/Flash-Lite models support **agentic video understanding** (the model navigates the timeline and loads only needed frames/audio/transcript). Default sampling is 1 FPS; use a custom higher fps for fast motion (FPS games). Timestamps can drift on very long videos: chunk (~10–20 min) and offset, or re-encode to constant fps. | docs/signals.md:18 — The result is a score-ranked list of `Candidate(start, end, score, signals, events)` dataclasses. `to_dict()` produces JSON-compatible dictionaries. Times are seconds from the beginning of the video; end is exclusive. Ties sort by start time. `signals` contains the maximum per-second **z-score** for each feature within the window; `score` is the maximum weighted interest in that window (not a probability). The CLI writes only JSON to stdout, optional-dependency warnings to stderr, and returns 2 on invalid input/decoder errors. Silent static input returns `[]`. Nothing calls Gemini, accesses a network, downloads weights, or modifies the input. | docs/stats.md:105 — Results include `jobs`, `duration_seconds`, `kills`, `deaths`, `kills_per_hour`, `deaths_per_hour`, `multikills`, `multikill_counts`, `character_usage`, `most_common_character`, `best_plays`, and `roast_worthy_fails`. Rates divide observed attributed feed events by total included recording hours, not by clip duration.
